LESSON: WRITING 6.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are stories important in communities?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write a story on the theme from artistic expressions
2. enjoy picture reading for creative writing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 6.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 6.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Write a story on the theme from artistic expressions

What this means
In this part you learn to write a story on the theme from artistic expressions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a story on the theme from artistic expressions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a story on the theme from artistic expressions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Enjoy picture reading for creative writing

What this means
In this part you learn to enjoy picture reading for creative writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: enjoy picture reading for creative writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can enjoy picture reading for creative writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: write a story on the theme from artistic expressions)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing to a partner. (skill: enjoy picture reading for creative writing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: write a story on the theme from artistic expressions.
3. Practise this skill: enjoy picture reading for creative writing.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are stories important in communities?
2. What is the importance of artistic work in expressing creativity?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: write a story on the theme from artistic expressions.
5. Be able to: enjoy picture reading for creative writing.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
